app: Exam Question Generator with Quality Check

questions.question: Which CPU scheduling algorithm gives the lowest average waiting time among all non-preemptive algorithms?
questions.explanation: Shortest Job First (SJF) is proven to yield the lowest average waiting time for any set of non-preemptive processes. FCFS suffers from the convoy effect, Round Robin is preemptive, and Priority scheduling does not guarantee optimal average waiting time.

questions.question: What scheduling phenomenon occurs in First-Come First-Served (FCFS) scheduling when short processes are forced to wait behind a single long process?
questions.explanation: The convoy effect occurs in non-preemptive FCFS scheduling when multiple short processes wait in the ready queue behind one CPU-bound long process, resulting in lower CPU and device utilization.

questions.question: If the time quantum in a Round Robin (RR) scheduling algorithm is set extremely high, the algorithm degenerates into First-Come First-Served (FCFS).
questions.explanation: When the time quantum of Round Robin becomes exceptionally large, processes complete their CPU bursts before the quantum expires, causing RR to behave exactly like FCFS.

questions.question: In priority scheduling, low-priority processes may suffer from starvation. Explain how the technique of 'ageing' resolves this issue.
questions.answer: Ageing gradually increases the priority of processes that wait in the ready queue for long periods. As a process spends more time waiting, its priority rises until it becomes high enough to gain CPU execution time, thereby preventing starvation.
questions.explanation: Ageing addresses indefinite blocking/starvation by making process priority a function of time spent waiting, guaranteeing that every process eventually gets executed.

questions.question: What is the primary operational trade-off when selecting a very small time quantum for a Round Robin CPU scheduler?
options: The algorithm degenerates to non-preemptive Shortest Job First.
Low-priority processes will experience complete starvation.
The short-term scheduler becomes completely unnecessary.
questions.explanation: If the time quantum is set too small, the system spends a disproportionate amount of time context switching relative to actual process execution time, degrading overall system throughput.
